title: Grade 2 Science — Fri, Jun 27
description: Animals and Their Young Ones — Day 5 of 5: Mixed review
subject: science

questions.question: Which animal is oviparous (lays eggs)?
questions.explanation: Parrots are birds — they lay eggs (oviparous). Dogs, cows and horses are viviparous (give birth to live young).

questions.question: What is a baby goat called?
questions.explanation: A baby goat is called a kid. Calves are baby cows, foals are baby horses and lambs are baby sheep.

questions.question: A mother dog feeds her puppies milk. This shows that dogs are:
questions.explanation: Feeding young with milk is a feature of mammals. Dogs are mammals — they give birth to live young and feed them milk.

questions.question: Which sound does a lion make?
questions.explanation: Lions roar. Dogs bark, sheep bleat and cows moo.

questions.question: A group of bees is called a:
questions.explanation: A group of bees is called a colony. They live in hives and have a very organized social structure.

questions.question: Tiger cubs stay with their mother for about 2 years. What does this tell us about parental care in tigers?
options: Tigers do not care for their young
Tiger mothers provide long-term care to teach cubs survival skills
questions.explanation: Tiger mothers spend 2+ years teaching cubs to hunt and survive. This is intensive parental care — not just feeding, but teaching life skills.

questions.question: A hen is oviparous. After her eggs hatch, she gathers the chicks under her wings. This shows:
options: Oviparous animals never care for young
Even oviparous animals can show parental care after birth/hatching
questions.explanation: Oviparous animals can still show parental care after eggs hatch. A hen keeping chicks warm is an example of post-hatching parental care.

questions.question: Match correctly: Cow → ___, Dog → ___, Hen → ___
questions.explanation: Cow → Calf. Dog → Puppy. Hen → Chick. These are the correct baby names for each animal.

questions.question: Which statement is FALSE?
options: A baby cat is called a kitten
Elephants give birth to live young
questions.explanation: Not all animals live in groups. Tigers, leopards and many other animals are solitary. The other three statements are all true.

questions.question: Animals in a herd (like zebras) alert each other when a predator is near by making sounds. What kind of behaviour is this?
options: Communication within a group for safety
questions.explanation: When one zebra sees a lion and makes a warning sound, others run. This is group communication for safety — one of the key advantages of living in herds.

questions.question: Which correctly lists one oviparous and one viviparous animal?
questions.explanation: Frogs lay eggs (oviparous). Dogs give birth to puppies (viviparous). The other pairs have the classifications swapped or wrong.

questions.question: A tadpole breathes through gills like a fish. An adult frog breathes through lungs and skin. What does this major change tell us?
options: The same animal can have completely different body structures at different life stages (metamorphosis)
questions.explanation: Metamorphosis means a complete change in body form. A tadpole and adult frog look and breathe differently yet are the same species at different life stages.

questions.question: Ants are oviparous. A queen ant lays thousands of eggs. Worker ants then care for the eggs and larvae. This shows:
options: Oviparous insects have no parental care
Parental care can be provided by non-parent community members
Oviparous animals always look after their own eggs
questions.explanation: Worker ants (who are not parents) care for the queen's eggs. This shows that parental care can come from the wider community, not just parents.

questions.question: Why do some animals (like turtles) lay hundreds of eggs while others (like elephants) have only one baby at a time?
options: Animals that give no parental care lay many eggs so some survive; animals with intensive care need fewer young
It depends on what they eat
questions.explanation: Turtles lay many eggs and abandon them — most won't survive, but some will. Elephants invest years of care in each calf, so even one calf has a very high chance of survival.

questions.question: Compare: 'Animals that live alone' vs 'Animals that live in groups'. Which is ALWAYS true?
options: Solitary animals are always predators; group animals are always prey
Living in a group always means more safety
Each survival strategy (solitary or group) has advantages depending on the animal's environment and food habits
questions.explanation: Neither strategy is universally better. Solitary animals like tigers are apex predators who don't need a pack. Social animals like wolves need cooperation. Each strategy suits different environments and food habits.
